name: Corallinum
origin: Calcareous skeleton of the red coral colony from the Mediterranean Sea and adjacent eastern Atlantic
habitat: Marine; rocky seabed of the Mediterranean and neighbouring Atlantic waters
partUsed: Dried calcareous skeleton of the coral colony
preparation: Trituration of the dried red coral skeleton, followed by attenuations
chemicalConstituents: Iron oxide (responsible for the red colour)
generalAnalysis: A marine animal remedy whose traditional picture is chiefly respiratory: profuse coryza, epistaxis and a dry, spasmodic, suffocative cough in very rapid paroxysms that almost run into one another. The face becomes purple during the cough, there is a sensation of smothering before the attack and great exhaustion afterwards, and the air passages feel intensely sensitive to cold air.

drugPicture.generalPicture: A picture of violent, rapid coughing. The attack is preceded by a sense of smothering, the paroxysms follow so closely that they almost merge, the face becomes purple, and the patient is exhausted afterwards. There is much coryza, post-nasal mucus and epistaxis, and inspired air feels icy cold.
